Replace the secret of a personal access token, or of a deploy token with --repo

Replace the secret of a token and show the new secret once. The old secret
stops working at once, so every client that uses it breaks until it gets the
new one.

Without --repo this rotates one of YOUR PERSONAL ACCESS TOKENS (see rp token
list). The new token keeps the name, the scopes and the expiry of the old one;
none of them can be changed here (an expired token comes back with 365 days
from now). It has a NEW id, which rp prints and puts in the structured output
as "id": revoke it with that id. It works with a login, a browser sign-in or a
personal access token, also one in REPSY_TOKEN (RPS-2440). A token whose scopes
the credential in use does not cover is refused (403) and nothing changes.

With --repo &lt;name&gt; this rotates a DEPLOY TOKEN of that repository. The server
answers only the new secret, not the username, so the structured output has an
empty username; the username of the token does not change (see rp token list
--repo &lt;name&gt;). Repsy Cloud also gives the token a new id (Repsy OS keeps it)
and does not say which: rp finds it by listing the tokens before and after,
prints it, and puts it in the structured output as "id". If it cannot be told,
rp says so and the id is empty.

rp asks for confirmation on a terminal; in a script pass --yes. The secret is
printed like in rp token create (--show-secret, or --output json|yaml / --jq).

```
NEW=$(rp token rotate <token-id> --yes --show-secret)
rp token rotate <token-id> --repo libs --yes --output json --jq .token
```

```
rp token rotate <token-id> [flags]
```

## Options

```
      --repo string   Rotate a deploy token of this repository (without it: a personal access token)
      --show-secret   Print the new secret on stdout (once); implied by a structured --output
```
